title: Treacle Tart
subtitle: Golden syrup and breadcrumb tart in a shortcrust case
excerpt: A rich, sweet British tart with a filling of golden syrup, fresh breadcrumbs, and lemon juice baked in a crisp shortcrust case. Dense, sticky, and very satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Treacle tart is one of the most distinctively British desserts. Despite the name, the filling uses golden syrup rather than black treacle: Lyle's Golden Syrup was invented in London in the 1880s and quickly became the defining sweetener for this tart. The breadcrumbs absorb the syrup and set the filling to a firm but sticky consistency; without them, the filling would be too liquid to slice. The amount of lemon juice is a matter of taste: more lemon sharpens the sweetness and provides relief from the richness. Harry Potter's favourite dessert, which contributed to a revival of interest in the dish in the 1990s and 2000s. Served warm with clotted cream, custard, or vanilla ice cream.

content.text: Warm the golden syrup gently before measuring it: this makes it much easier to pour and ensures it combines evenly with the breadcrumbs. Make fresh breadcrumbs by blitzing slightly stale white bread in a food processor. The tart should be set around the edges but still have a slight wobble in the centre when you remove it from the oven: it will firm up as it cools.

Heat the oven to 190 C / fan 170 C / gas 5. Roll out the pastry on a lightly floured surface and line a 23 cm tart tin. Trim the edges and chill for 20 minutes. Line with baking paper and baking beans and blind-bake for 15 minutes. Remove the paper and beans and bake for a further 5 minutes until pale golden.

Reduce the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Warm the golden syrup in a saucepan over low heat until runny. Remove from the heat and stir in the breadcrumbs, lemon juice, zest, and cream. Mix until combined.

Pour the filling into the pastry case. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the filling is set around the edges but still very slightly wobbly in the centre. Cool for at least 20 minutes before slicing. Serve warm with clotted cream, custard, or vanilla ice cream.
